author: Alex Whitney
title: Pritzker unveils 'Fighting for Illinois: Day One Agenda' for Congress - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Whitney ,
3 hours ago
ILLINOIS (WCIA) -- Governor Pritzker is urging his Congressional Democrats to hit the ground running when they return to Washington.
He is calling on the party to use its newly won control of the House and Senate to advance an aggressive legislative agenda looking to counter changes made by the Trump administration and his previous Republican majority in DC over the last two years.
JB Pritzker projected winner in race for Illinois Governor Pritzker's plan offers hundreds of policy recommendations and executive actions that he believes Democrats should advance, like increasing the federal minimum wage, reversing cuts to SNAP and Medicaid programs and restoring staffing at agencies like the Department of Education.
Pritzker's Deputy Governor for Education, Martin Torres, said the impacts of Trump's Big Beautiful Bill on students, particularly student borrowers, has been devastating.
"They eliminated the grad student loan program in H.R. 1. They lowered the aggregate cap on graduate loans that people can take out. They eliminated nurse practitioners and physician's assistance from the people who could take out loans to pursue a profession or degree. And so, we've seen opportunities limited for Illinois students across the state," said Torres.
Torres said Democrats should keep students in mind when prioritizing what issues to tackle first in the new Congress.
He said voters made it clear they expect lawmakers to tackle issues of affordability and he believes the economic mobility that comes with a degree could help address those.
"When you have a comprehensive 200 points playbook for Congress to take up, it's a wide array of issues. Senator elect Juliana Stratton today answered a question to a reporter and said, we can walk and chew gum. I expect Congress to be able to address a number of issues come currently when they reconvene. Education is about economic mobility, but education is also about building the workforce that we need to be competitive And so it's it is of the utmost importance for the federal government to address the issues that the Trump administration has caused and how these limited opportunities for not only Illinois students and students across the country," said Torres.
